newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour to keep inheritance, capital gains taxes.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour to keep inheritance, capital gains taxes.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour party would reintroduce inheritance and capital gains tax if they were abolished by the ruling Conservatives and use the revenue to cut the basic rate of income tax, a senior aide to shadow finance minister Gordon Brown said.

Cutting the starting rate of tax to 15 or even 10 percent would be a key Labour priority, alongside the abolition of value-added tax on fuel, the aide, who asked not to be named, told reporters at the Labour party conference.
The aide said there was a possibility that Prime Minister John Major might announce the abolition of capital gains and inheritance tax at the Conservative party conference next week.
"If he does we will reverse it in our first budget," he said.

Labour was anxious to make a start in reducing the high marginal rate of taxes paid by the poor by reforming the tax and benefit system but the extent of any move would depend on the state of public finances it inherited.
The welfare benefits which the lowest-paid receive to supplement their incomes would be adjusted to make sure they received the benefit of a lower starting tax rate, the aide said.
